newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower; downtrend seen.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower; downtrend seen.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Tuesday amid a lack of bullish factors to help the market extend its recent gains, and brokers said they saw a downward consolidation ahead.
The weighted index ended 71.40 points or 0.87 percent lower at 8,123.26.
Turnover was a muted T$73.60 billion.
Before Tuesday's session, the index had gained nearly 200 points since May 15 in a modest rebound fuelled by investors buying up bargains after a big April-May correction.
"The fact is the rebound was mostly technical and the market lacks a concrete reason to rise further," said Allen Huang, a fund manager for National Securities.
Trading on Tuesday focused heavily on the electronic sector, which included four of the five most heavily traded shares.
Chipmaker Winbond gained T$1.10 to T$38.90 and computer giant Acer Inc rose T$0.50 to T$76.50.
But electronic sector as a whole suffered profit-taking, losing 1.29 percent.
"Electronics had been rebounding from a previous round of selling, but now they are hitting a wall again," Huang said.
Brokers said they expected the index to continue a slow descent, with firm support not seen until the 7,800 level.
A 8,020-8,150 range was seen for Wednesday.
